title: A fresh morning
text: I open the window and make a cup of tea. A quiet morning helps me start the day with a clear mind.
cues: Stress the words quiet and clear.

title: Asking for directions
text: Excuse me, could you tell me the way to the station? I'm looking for the entrance near the river.

title: A lunch invitation
text: Would you like to have lunch with us? We're making vegetable noodles, and there's enough for everyone.
cues: Say the final sound in noodles.

title: Time for a break
text: I've been sitting at this desk for a long time. I think a short walk would help me return with more energy.

title: A practical proposal
text: We should review the feedback before changing the design. A small improvement could make the service much easier to use.

title: Technology for everyone
text: An accessible website should offer clear instructions and predictable navigation. Convenience means little if some people cannot participate.
cues: Break the first sentence into sense groups.

title: Our shared environment
text: Protecting a local habitat requires patience and cooperation. The results may be gradual, but consistent effort can create lasting change.

title: Learning with curiosity
text: I don't need to understand every word immediately. When I stay curious and ask questions, difficult ideas become easier to explore.
cues: Expand don't to do not if needed.
Finish the final consonant in questions.

title: A routine that works for you
text: Describe a daily routine that helps you feel organized.

title: A memorable journey
text: Talk about a journey you enjoyed, even if it was close to home.
cues: Where did you go and with whom?
What would you do differently next time?

title: A dish to share
text: Describe a dish you would prepare for a visiting friend.
cues: Why is it special to you?

title: Making space for rest
text: Explain how people can make time for rest in a busy week.
cues: Give an example from everyday life.

title: Your ideal team
text: Describe what makes a team pleasant and effective to work with.
cues: How can a team handle disagreement?
Share a real or imagined example.

title: One useful digital tool
text: Discuss a digital tool that saves you time and one limitation it has.
cues: How often do you use it?
When would another approach be better?

title: A greener neighborhood
text: Propose a realistic environmental project for your neighborhood.
cues: What local problem would it address?

title: Learning beyond the classroom
text: Compare learning from a course with learning through personal projects.
cues: Explain one advantage of each approach.
Recommend a combination for a beginner.
